$comment: Create a standard sales order with VA01 in SAP GUI for HTML. The catalog entry opens VA01 directly (start page #Shell-startGUI?sap-ui2-tcode=VA01). Steps: initial screen, header data, one item, save. Field selectors use the SAP GUI field tooltips (title attribute), case-insensitive, with alternatives for different releases. If a field is not found the step is shown in the middle of the screen, so the text still tells the user what to do. Re-pick a field in the tour editor if it is not highlighted on your system.

steps.title: Create a sales order
steps.text:
This tour walks you through creating a standard sales order with transaction VA01 (Create Sales Documents):

  1. Choose the order type and sales area
  2. Enter the customer and the purchase order number
  3. Add the material and quantity
  4. Save the order

You type the values yourself; the tour shows you where.

steps.title: Order type
steps.text: Enter the order type. A standard order is OR. If your company uses its own order type, type that one and choose Next.

steps.title: Sales organization
steps.text: Enter the sales organization that sells to this customer, for example 1010.

steps.title: Distribution channel
steps.text: Enter the distribution channel, for example 10 (direct sales). Press F4 in the field to see the allowed values.

steps.title: Division
steps.text: Enter the division, for example 00. Sales organization, distribution channel and division together are the sales area.

steps.title: Go to the order
steps.text:
Press Enter on your keyboard or click the green check mark to open the order overview.
Pressed the Enter key? Choose Next once the next screen appears.

steps.title: Sold-to party
steps.text: Enter the customer number of the customer who orders. Don't know it? Press F4 in the field to search by name.

target.selector: [title='Sold-To Party' i], [title='Sold-to party number' i], [title='Customer number of sold-to party' i]

steps.title: Ship-to party
steps.text: Where the goods go. Leave it empty to use the sold-to party's address: SAP fills it in when you press Enter.

steps.title: Customer reference
steps.text: Enter the customer's purchase order number, so the customer recognizes the order on the order confirmation and the invoice.

target.selector: [title='Customer Reference' i], [title='Cust. Reference' i], [title^='Customer purchase order number' i], [title='Purchase order no.' i]

steps.title: Requested delivery date
steps.text: Enter the date the customer wants the goods. SAP checks later whether the material can be delivered by then.

target.selector: [title='Requested delivery date' i], [title='Req. Deliv.Date' i], [title='Req. Deliv. Date' i]

steps.title: Material
steps.text: In the first item row, enter the material number. Press F4 to search for a material.

steps.title: Order quantity
steps.text: Enter how many the customer orders, in the sales unit (for example PC).

target.selector: [title='Order Quantity' i], [title^='Cumulative Order Quantity' i], [title='Order Qty' i]

steps.title: Check the item
steps.text: Press Enter. SAP fills in the description, price and availability for the item. If a popup appears (for example for availability), confirm it. Add more items in the next rows the same way, then choose Next.

steps.title: Save the order
steps.text: When everything is right, click Save (or press Ctrl+S).

steps.title: Order created
steps.text:
The status bar at the bottom shows Standard Order ... has been saved with the new order number. Note it down or give it to the customer.

To change or display the order later, use VA02 or VA03.
